Read a climate raster with its context

Source: R/read_climate.R
read_climate.Rd

Reads one or more raster files and records what later steps need: the dates of the layers, the variable, its unit, the time step and whether the values are continuous, counts or categories. Layers are named by their ISO dates. Explicit arguments always win over what the files say.

Usage

read_climate(
  path,
  variable = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  time_step = NULL,
  kind = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  na_value = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  rotate = TRUE
)

Arguments

path

Path(s) to raster files, or a SpatRaster.

variable

Variable name, e.g. "tmax" or "pre".

unit

Unit of the values, e.g. "K" or "mm/day". This declares the unit; to change the values, use convert_unit().

time_step

One of "hour", "day", "month", "year". Inferred from the dates when NULL.

kind

One of "continuous", "count", "categorical". Decides how later steps aggregate the values (mean, sum, mode). Inferred from the variable when NULL.

source

Name of a registered source, to skip detection.

na_value

Values to treat as missing, e.g. 128 for URCA.

label

Name used in progress messages and later steps. Defaults to the file name.

rotate

When TRUE, rotate rasters with longitudes beyond 180.

Value

A SpatRaster with dates, unit and package metadata; see raster_meta().

Details

Dates come, in order of preference, from the source's convention (ERA5 layer names such as t2m_valid_time=1704067200), from the dates stored in the file, from layer names that are dates, or from dates in the file names when there is one file per layer (CHIRPS). The variable is taken from the source or found in the variable and file names, and is standardised: t2m becomes tmean, tp and precip become pre. See register_source() to add a dataset's conventions.

While reading, codes in na_value become NA, and a raster with longitudes from 0 to 360 is rotated to -180 to 180 so it lines up with survey coordinates.

See also

raster_meta(), aggregate_time(), convert_unit()

Examples

tmax <- read_climate(
  system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
#> Read tmax_daily: tmax [K], daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 1095 layers
#> (synthetic).
raster_meta(tmax)[c("variable", "unit", "time_step")]
#> $variable
#> [1] "tmax"
#> 
#> $unit
#> [1] "K"
#> 
#> $time_step
#> [1] "day"
#>
